title: ERP Database Access
html:
ADR-0033 records the owner's definitive decision. This policy covers external ERPs, not IA-MNS's own PostgreSQL migration/runtime separation.

Exactly two access identities per ERP

ERP Runtime reader Administration and Discovery
Sankhya / Oracle IA_MNS_RO, provisioned with verified reads under PH-08 Existing administrative user, also used by Codex
VRMaster / PostgreSQL ia_mns, already provisioned under PH-19 Existing administrative user, also used by Codex

Do not create a third Discovery-only account. The administrator retains its existing purpose and privileges; finishing Discovery does not require deletion or password rotation. Rotate for an actual credential-lifecycle or exposure reason under secrets management, with appropriate owner authority.

Runtime gets only the objects/projections needed by enabled application capabilities. Oracle requires CREATE SESSION, reviewed object SELECT and name resolution; no broad ANY privileges, DML, DDL or procedure execution. PostgreSQL requires database CONNECT, schema USAGE and reviewed table/column SELECT, without ownership, superuser or write privileges. Actual inherited PUBLIC CREATE/TEMP permissions currently exceed that intended boundary; the owner instructed preserving PUBLIC while PH-30 tracks coordinated restriction. Do not claim effective DDL denial for this account. A read-only transaction supplements these grants.

Credential delivery

Normal .env.local and deployment contain only runtime SANKHYA_DB_USER / SANKHYA_DB_PASSWORD and VRMASTER_DB_USER / VRMASTER_DB_PASSWORD, plus non-secret connection settings. Keep the existing administrative pairs in an ignored root Discovery file. Tools prefer .env.discovery.local when present and otherwise use the owner-selected .env.discovery; they never merge the two files:

  • VRMASTER_DB_USER_FULLACESS and VRMASTER_DB_PASSWORD_FULLACESS (preserved spelling).
  • SANKHYA_DB_USER_FULLACESS and SANKHYA_DB_PASSWORD_FULLACESS.

The safe example contains no actual account values. Protect the real file with the owner's local access controls. Never commit it, print it, attach it to chat, include it in an image/backup for distribution, send it to a model, or load it through Node/Vite runtime environment flags. Do not place administrative credentials in runtime-named keys.

The local loader excludes all four administrative keys before spawning development commands, including phone-test processes. It never reads .env.discovery.local. The runtime parser refuses those keys if externally injected into a directly started runtime. The Discovery loader selects and reads one administrative file explicitly without putting its values in process.env, accepts only those four keys, requires development/test configuration and never falls back to runtime credentials. Administrative settings are deliberately absent from the runtime schema/reference and public configuration.

These controls separate delivery. They do not certify privileges behind a runtime-named credential. Sankhya products retain their existing privilege/ownership check; existing sales and directory readers use fixed read-only queries and rely on DBA-verified grants. Do not claim an unprovisioned Oracle reader is ready because configuration parses.

Discovery authority and confidentiality

Codex may investigate objects needed for development without requesting fresh approval for each read. Use reviewed SELECT/catalog inspection, explicit minimal columns, bound values, bounded rows/connections and timeouts. Use read-only transactions where applicable and always roll back/close sessions. Read-only transactions, a SELECT prefix check and fixed queries are not a sufficient sandbox for administrative credentials; review the target objects and any functions/views for side effects before use.

Do not execute INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE, DDL, GRANT, REVOKE, write-capable procedures, maintenance commands or any other ERP state change during Discovery. This applies even in a transaction intended for rollback. Technical privilege is not authorization. A database mutation requires explicit owner authorization for its target and operation; a Discovery authorization is never mutation approval.

Credentials are RESTRICTED. ERP business data is CONFIDENTIAL and personal fields need concrete task justification. Do not send confidential raw rows, credentials or unnecessary personal information to AI models. Inspect data locally, prefer counts/structural evidence, redact/minimize any shared evidence, and use synthetic model/test inputs where possible. Ignored evidence is still confidential data requiring controlled local access and retention under classification and retention. Model-assisted regressions require their existing, separately reviewed minimized product input boundary; they must not transmit discovery exports or administrative configuration.

Available development tools

The setup procedure owns commands. erp:discovery inspects one named object with fixed Oracle/PostgreSQL metadata queries and optional explicit-column samples of at most 100 rows. It accepts no arbitrary SQL or model-generated query. Metadata and data are written only to ignored apps/api/evals/.local/discovery; console output contains status/counts only. It is not a general SQL sandbox or a privilege verifier.

Sankhya products:sankhya:sync and products:sankhya:regression explicitly use the existing administrator by default; --runtime-check / --runtime use only the reader and never load the administrative file. VRMaster products:catalog and products:regression continue using the runtime reader to verify its actual visibility and behavior; they do not silently switch to the administrator.

New runtime access and activation

For a new capability, identify the minimum object/column privileges, name resolution, reason and affected queries; prepare repository-reviewed scripts targeted only at IA_MNS_RO or ia_mns. Keep Discovery metadata candidates separate from enabled runtime paths. Execute scripts only within explicit owner mutation authority and then verify effective grants and reconcile runtime reads without probing writes. Report missing provisioning or authorization through the relevant Human Action.

The owner separately authorized and completed the current Runtime access provisioning: reviewed Oracle SELECT/name-resolution/directory changes and three PostgreSQL column grants. erp:runtime:access inspects the current plan by default; --apply is a mutation mode requiring explicit owner authority, never ordinary Discovery. The canonical templates target the existing readers and do not change accounts/passwords. Oracle DDL is not transactionally reversible; PostgreSQL grants use one transaction. Read-only inspection never automatically executes a grant or changes an account.
